insights.topic: Verified purchase proof vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: Crinkl's cryptographically verified receipts represent deterministic purchase confirmation — a structurally different signal from cookie-based inference. At ~$0.10 per verified receipt, the cost of confirmed purchase data is a fraction of the $5+ CPM brands pay to infer purchase intent from behavioral proxies.

14-day data shows grocery-supermarkets leading by receipt volume (1,407 receipts) while retail-department-stores leads by GMV ($35,039 vs. $60,361 across 614 fewer receipts) — a confirmed higher average ticket in retail. Brands targeting either channel have category-level purchase verification, not modeled audience segments.

The top three brands by 14-day receipt count — Walmart (314), Costco Wholesale (138), Kroger (137) — account for a disproportionate share of verified grocery GMV. For CPG brands seeking verified in-store purchase data at scale, concentration in these three retailers is the current reality of where verified receipt volume actually lives.

7-Eleven, Circle K, and Dollar General crossed the receipt-density visibility threshold within a 168-hour window after a 40+ snapshot brand-list freeze — signaling a real expansion of verified coverage into gas-convenience and value retail, two channels historically underserved by purchase verification data.

insights.topic: Daily GMV run rate and network scale
insights.insight: Implied daily verified GMV is running $13,700–$14,200 across roughly 19 metro areas, with cumulative receipts exceeding 96,000. This is an early-stage network — useful for signal validation and audience testing, not yet a replacement for national-scale purchase panels.

insights.topic: Settlement lag as a data-freshness constraint
insights.insight: 809 confirmed payouts have been static for 60+ consecutive snapshots, indicating verified receipts carry a non-trivial settlement hold before they clear. Brands evaluating this data for real-time campaign optimization should account for the lag between purchase event and confirmed verification — this is a near-real-time signal, not an instant one.
